questions.q: Which four defaults does Parrish say get in the way of clear thinking?
a: Emotion, ego, social pressure and inertia
Fear, anger, pride and fatigue
Bias, habit, stress and distraction
Doubt, denial, urgency and optimism
questions.why: Lesson 1 names the emotion, ego, social and inertia defaults as the primary enemies of clear thinking.

questions.q: What happens when several of these defaults fire at once?
a: Thinking breaks down completely and bad decisions follow
They cancel each other out and restore calm
The strongest default takes over harmlessly
We notice the pattern and correct it quickly
questions.why: The summary says that when the defaults act together, all hell breaks loose, as in the story of the angry CEO.

questions.q: What does Parrish mean by self-accountability?
a: Owning your mistakes and the bad luck that isn't your fault
Tracking how often your predictions turn out right
Accepting blame only when you clearly caused the problem
Letting others take responsibility for team failures
questions.why: Lesson 2 says self-accountability means taking responsibility for your errors and for bad situations you did not cause.

questions.q: What is the first step in Parrish's process for handling a mistake?
a: Accept your share of responsibility for what happened
Explain why the mistake was unavoidable
Wait until the damage becomes completely clear
Ask someone else to fix the problem
questions.why: The four-step process starts with accepting responsibility, even when your share of the cause is small or nonexistent.

questions.q: What does Parrish call the bigger mistake people make after an error?
a: Trying to hide it and dodge responsibility
Apologizing too quickly and too often
Changing the plan before it has been tested
Refusing to try anything risky again
questions.why: The summary quotes Parrish saying the first mistake is expensive, but covering it up costs a fortune.
